title: Kani Township Humanitarian Emergency: 30,900+ Civilians Displaced from 44 Villages as SAC Airstrike and Ground Campaign Intensifies
detail: As of May 13, 2026, the ongoing SAC airstrike and ground column operations in Kani Township, Sagaing Region, have displaced over 30,900 civilians from 44 villages since the campaign began in late April 2026, according to Moemaka CDM Domestic News. The displacement figure represents one of the largest single-township forced displacement events in 2026 and reflects the scale of junta operations since launching its Yinmabin-Pale-Kani multi-township ground invasion on May 1. The SAC has combined air attacks — hitting a hospital on May 7 (killing 2 PDF) and several residential areas — with armored ground columns that have raided and burned villages throughout the township. With 30,900+ displaced unable to access proper food, clean water, or shelter during extreme hot-season temperatures (May temperatures in central Myanmar often exceed 40°C), UN humanitarian alerts classify this as a life-threatening emergency. The junta's Kani campaign is strategically linked to its broader effort to clear the lower Sagaing-Magway border corridor of resistance forces following the January-March 2026 PDF gains in the area. MoeMaKa's CDM network — documenting displacement township by township — also recorded 4 civilians killed and 7 injured in Kani Township operations to date.

media.caption: 30,900+ civilians displaced from 44 villages in Kani Township, Sagaing Region, as junta airstrikes and ground columns intensify — May 13, 2026

title: Resistance Forces Ambush Junta Troop Column in Magway Region — 6 SAC Soldiers Killed, 30+ Injured
detail: Resistance forces in Magway Region conducted a guerrilla ambush on a Myanmar junta troop contingent on May 13, 2026, killing 6 soldiers and injuring more than 30, according to Mizzima's Spring Revolution Daily News. The Magway ambush occurred amid the SAC's intensifying ground offensive in Pauk and Saw townships, which launched large-scale operations on May 13-14. The 30+ injured figure represents one of the higher single-operation injury tolls for SAC forces in Magway Region in 2026. The attack is consistent with PDF guerrilla strategy in Magway: using ambushes and mines to attrite SAC column strength and degrade the junta's capacity to sustain ground operations in the region. Magway Region has seen intensifying PDF activity since late April 2026, when PDF forces ambushed and killed approximately 25 SAC troops on the Myingyan-Nyaung-U road (April 28) and a PDF mine attack destroyed a junta convoy carrying aerial bombs in Seik Phyu Township (May 9). On the same day as the ambush, mine attacks also struck junta forces departing Salingyi and Yinmabin towns in Sagaing Region, killing and injuring an unspecified but reportedly 'large number' of soldiers.

media.caption: Resistance forces ambush and kill 6 junta soldiers, injure 30+ in Magway Region — Spring Revolution Daily News, Mizzima, May 13, 2026

title: Ye Balu Resistance Force Assassinates SAC Deputy Battalion Commander Tun Yar Kyaw in Ye Township, Mon State
detail: The Ye Balu resistance force shot and killed Tun Yar Kyaw, the second commander (deputy battalion commander) of Myanmar junta unit Ka-La-Ya (106) based in Lamai, in the Lamaing police station area of Ye Township, Mon State, on approximately May 11-13, 2026, according to Mizzima's Spring Revolution Daily News and Moemaka CDM. The killing of an officer-grade junta commander is notable for the Ye Township area — Mon State's southernmost major township bordering Tanintharyi Region — which has been an increasingly active PDF/resistance zone throughout 2025-2026. The Ye Balu Force has been one of the more active resistance units operating in Mon State's southern corridor. The PDFs in Mon State operate in coordination with KNLA (Karen National Liberation Army) forces to the east, creating overlapping pressure on SAC positions in the region. The targeted killing of a deputy battalion commander reflects the resistance's increasingly effective tactical intelligence — identifying and eliminating high-value targets within SAC unit command structures rather than mass infantry engagements. This follows the April 7, 2026 PDF ambush in Ye Township that killed one SAC officer and two soldiers.

media.caption: Ye Balu Force kills SAC deputy battalion commander Tun Yar Kyaw (Ka-La-Ya 106 unit) in Ye Township, Mon State — Mizzima Spring Revolution Daily News, May 13, 2026

title: NUG Calls on ASEAN and International Community to Adopt 'Clear, Time-Bound Benchmarks' for Cessation of Junta Airstrikes
detail: Myanmar's National Unity Government (NUG) formally called on ASEAN, the United Nations, and the international community on May 13, 2026, to reject junta legitimacy and adopt 'clear, time-bound benchmarks for the cessation of airstrikes,' according to Mizzima. The NUG statement came days after the 46th ASEAN Summit in Kuala Lumpur (May 7-9), where ASEAN foreign ministers agreed to hold a virtual meeting with Myanmar's junta-installed foreign minister — the first formal political engagement since the SAC was excluded from ASEAN meetings in 2021. The NUG framed the ASEAN decision as rewarding impunity and called for a fundamentally different international posture: concrete demands with measurable outcomes rather than process-oriented dialogue. The same day, the UN's Independent Investigative Mechanism for Myanmar (IIMM) marked the first anniversary of the May 12, 2025 Depayin school bombing — which killed 22 children and 2 teachers — with a statement warning that children continue to face lethal airstrike threats in 2026. The NUG's benchmark demand reflects strategic escalation in its international advocacy posture: moving from calls for recognition to specific accountability mechanisms that would test whether ASEAN engagement produces any change in junta behavior. Min Aung Hlaing's government, inaugurated April 10, 2026, has maintained its airstrike campaign without pause — dropping over 15 bombs on Mindat and Kanpetlet (Chin State) in one day on May 15 — confirming the NUG's assessment that ASEAN engagement has not changed junta military conduct.

media.caption: NUG demands ASEAN adopt clear, time-bound benchmarks for cessation of junta airstrikes — Mizzima, May 13, 2026
